cards.title: One-Horned Rhinoceros
cards.blurb: Chitwan National Park holds the second largest population of the greater one-horned rhino. From under 100 animals in the 1960s, protection has brought the park's count back above 600.

cards.title: Royal Bengal Tiger
cards.blurb: Seeing one is mostly luck and pugmarks. The park's tigers move through tall elephant grass that stands higher than a person on foot.

cards.title: Gharial Crocodile
cards.blurb: The narrow-snouted fish eater of the Rapti and Narayani rivers, critically endangered. The breeding centre at Kasara raises and releases them each year.

cards.title: Dugout Canoe on the Rapti
cards.blurb: A hollowed sal-trunk canoe drifts past basking muggers and kingfishers at first light, with the Churia hills behind.

cards.title: Tharu Stick Dance
cards.blurb: The indigenous Tharu people of the inner Terai perform the lathi naach in a ring of drums, striking staves in time.

cards.title: Tharu Painted Mask
cards.blurb: Painted clay and papier-mâché masks from the villages around Sauraha, made for festival dances and sold at the roadside.

cards.title: Jungle Jeep Safari
cards.blurb: Take the jeep deep into the core area with a naturalist, or walk the buffer zone alone and hope the rhino is in a good mood. Roll for your sighting.

cards.title: Tharu Village Dinner
cards.blurb: Ghonghi snails, dhikri and bagiya served in a mud-walled Tharu home. Everyone at the table collects.

cards.title: Birding Count-Off
cards.blurb: Over 500 bird species live in the park. Challenge one traveller — highest roll logs the longer list.
